newsitem.title: USA: Henry Schein buys healthcare marketer.
newsitem.headline: Henry Schein buys healthcare marketer.

text.p: Henry Schein Inc said Tuesday it bought IDE Interstate Inc of Amityville, N.Y., for an undisclosed sum of cash.
The company said it expected to close the acquisition of the marketer of healthcare products within 90 days. IDE posted $50 million in revenues in 1996, Henry Schein said.
A spokeswoman said the company will not take a one-time charge to account for the acquisition, but amortize it over time.
"The acquisition will be accredive to earnings in 1998," Chief Financial Officer Steven Paladino told Reuters. "I can easily see a couple of pennies (added to earnings per share)."
Paladino called the acquisition "highly synergetic," saying IDE has a similar business to Henry Schein's core business.
Henry Schein on June 16 said it bought Health-Tech, a maker of dental practice management software, for an undisclosed price. The company said it would take a charge to account for the acquisition.
The company posted a $1.5 million net income, or $0.06 a share (including a $0.11 charge for the purchase of Dentrix Dental Systems Inc), on revenues of $240.5 million in the first quarter.
This compared with a net of $2.7 million, or $0.14 a share, on revenues of $187.4 million the year before.
Henry Schein's stock traded at 35-7/8 Tuesday afternoon, down 3/8.
